name: optimize_csharp_regex_compiled_per_call
description: Optimizes a validator that constructs a new Regex on every call to a single compiled instance
prompts: Validator.CountValid(string[] lines) in Validator.cs counts how many strings in lines match the email-like pattern `^user-\d+@example\.com$`. It constructs `new Regex(pattern)` INSIDE the loop, once per line - parsing and building the regex engine state for the same fixed pattern on every call is wasted work and makes the function far too slow for large inputs. Rewrite CountValid so the Regex is constructed ONCE (e.g. a static readonly field) and reused for every line, returning the exact same count. Keep the class name and the CountValid(string[]) signature.

setup_files.app.csproj:
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- tests/ has its own project; without this the SDK's default glob
         compiles tests/*.cs into the app itself, where xunit isn't referenced -->
    <Compile Remove="tests/**" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>
